title: docs(agents): generalise the shared-stash rule to all shared ref namespaces
body:
Closes #11946, closes #11273

## ⛔ Governed surface — this stays a draft

`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are governed faces (Prime Directive #14). This PR is deliberately a **draft**: not ready-flipped, no auto-merge, not in the merge queue. A human lands it. Green is necessary here, not sufficient.

## Per-item checklist

- [x] **#11946** — `AGENTS.md` §9 gains the general **four-namespace rule** beside the existing stash rule, the **three instances**, and the **four practices**; `CLAUDE.md`'s stash excerpt gains the one-sentence pointer that keeps it in sync.
- [x] **#11273** — the footer block gains the one clause the grading comment identified as still missing: a PR-**body** PATCH also **APPENDS** a platform bare footer, plus the explicit ⛔ don't-loop.
- [x] Ratchet ceilings **unchanged** — both files land exactly at their existing ceilings, paid by compression.
- [x] No hook added (per objectui#5700's binding reasoning).
- [x] No changeset (instruction files; publishes nothing).
- [x] No file under `content/docs/releases/` touched.

## #11946 — what the new text says

The existing stash rule teaches the right lesson at too narrow a scope. The general fact:

> A worktree isolates your **checkout** and exactly four ref namespaces — `HEAD`, `refs/bisect`, `refs/worktree`, `refs/rewritten`. It does **not** isolate the object store, the repo config, or any other ref.

`refs/stash` is one *case*. A reader who learns only the stash rule concludes "worktrees isolate refs, except stash" — the opposite of the truth — so the new paragraph names that misreading explicitly and adds the two further instances:

- **`refs/remotes/*`** — a sibling's fetch advances **your** `origin/main`, so a path-scoped `git checkout origin/main -- PATHS` restores wherever that ref points *now*, possibly newer than your branch base: another agent's merged work entering your tree under the name of a "revert". The path-scoped form also **stages** what it restores, which the existing staging rule immediately below then covers.
- **`FETCH_HEAD`** — the instance whose symptom is an **absence**, not wrong content: a `git diff` against a moved `FETCH_HEAD` exits 0 and prints nothing, which reads as *"the change is not there"* — a confidently wrong review conclusion on evidence that looks clean. Called out as worst for **reviewing** seats.

Then the four practices, stated as practices rather than prohibitions: pin `BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` at worktree creation and restore against that commit; verify a named remote-tracking ref's content by occurrence counts on disk; fetch into a ref you own (`git fetch origin BRANCH:refs/NAMESPACE/ID -f`) and read that; diff restored paths against `BASE` before staging.

### ⚠️ FETCH_HEAD is stated per CHECKOUT, not per worktree

Per the card's own binding correction, the landed text says **the last fetch in this checkout wins** and names the hazard site as the **shared primary checkout** — where every agent's first `git fetch` lands before it creates a worktree, and where reviewing seats work. The flat "`FETCH_HEAD` lives in the common `.git` dir and is shared by every worktree" wording is **not** used anywhere: objectui#6222 measured it false on git 2.43 (`git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD` resolves to `.git/worktrees/NAME/FETCH_HEAD` in a linked worktree; worktree B fetching a different branch did not move worktree A's). Repeating an unverified scope claim is precisely the error the parent card exists to correct.

### ⛔ No hook, by design

The safe forms are `git checkout` and `git fetch` — ordinary commands — and the unsafe spelling is legitimate elsewhere, so a mechanical block would fire on correct usage. objectui#5700's reasoning is binding; the new text says so. None added, none proposed.

## #11273 — the missing clause

The footer block already documented bare-stripped-on-PR-edit, session-URL survival, create-rewrites-bare, the comment-side append, and the ⛔ tail-bare-is-the-platform's rule. The one mechanism missing was this card's: **an edit also APPENDS a fresh platform bare footer under yours, and the next edit strips that one and appends another — so the floor is your session-URL footer plus one platform bare**, with the explicit ⛔ don't loop trying to normalize it. Two lines, folded into the existing `**PR body:**` sentence rather than added as a new paragraph.

## Paying for it — both files were at ZERO headroom

| file | ceiling | before | after | ceiling raised? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | 1149 | 1149 | **1149** | **no** |
| `CLAUDE.md` | 86 | 86 | **86** | **no** |

Net diff is **194 insertions / 194 deletions** — exactly zero lines added. The new material (~21 lines in `AGENTS.md`, ~2 in the footer block, ~3 in `CLAUDE.md`) is paid for by compressing §9 narrative in place, which is the payment the ratchet header names ("pays its way by moving narrative out or compressing in place, instead of raising the roof") and which the gate's own failure text prescribes: *"provenance is one line, stories live on cards, not in operational text."*

**What compression removed — incident colour only.** No rule, no ⛔/⚠️ directive, no gate name, no command, no file path, no maintainer ruling and no measured number was dropped. The `157`-deletion PR, the `MM` porcelain reading, the six required contexts, the 2026-08-12 deferral ruling, the ~18-merges-a-day figure and the 2026-08-20 footer measurement all survive verbatim. The prose trimmed is of this kind: item 2's "(how one implementation once got duplicated)", item 10's two worked examples of jointly-wrong merges, the actor rule's blow-by-blow, and rhetorical tails such as "That is why 'arm only on green' is a rule, not a formality."

⚠️ **The diff is wide for a two-card PR (340 touched lines in `AGENTS.md`) and that is inherent, not scope creep**: at zero headroom every added line must be found somewhere, and compression re-flows the paragraphs it shortens. Compression was confined to §9 — the section being edited — plus the two `CLAUDE.md` sections that excerpt it.

⛔ **No verbatim maintainer ruling was re-flowed** — zero 「…」 quotations appear on either side of the diff (checked), so `check-skill-frame-sync`'s failure mode is not in play. Line widths follow each block's own existing convention; lines were **not** widened toward the 120-byte cap to buy line count, which would defeat the byte rule's documented purpose.

## `CLAUDE.md` sync

`CLAUDE.md` excerpts the stash rule, and its section heading ("the stash stack is NOT covered by worktree isolation") invites exactly the wrong generalisation the card exists to correct. It gains one sentence — stash is one CASE, the four namespaces, `refs/remotes/*` is shared too, and a pointer to `AGENTS.md` §9 for the full rule — paid for inside `CLAUDE.md`'s own ceiling. The general rule is stated once, in `AGENTS.md`; `CLAUDE.md` carries the redirect, not a second copy.

## Gates

All run at final head **`bba3131a3`**, each exit code captured by redirect **before** any pipe, each quoted from the gate's own verdict line. The set was derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (which reads the changeset from the merge base itself), not from a hand-written list:

| gate | exit | verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| `check:pm-skill-ratchet` | 0 | `✓ AGENTS.md is 1149 lines (ceiling 1149; headroom 0).` / `✓ CLAUDE.md is 86 lines (ceiling 86; headroom 0).` |
| `check:pm-governed-prose` | 0 | `✓ 2 instruction surface(s) name all 5 registered governed surfaces … and claim no others.` |
| `check:docs-audit-scope` | 0 | `✓ docs-accuracy-audit scope is in sync with content/docs/: 189 hand-written doc(s).` |
| `check:agent-test-spelling` | 0 | `✓ 0 violations — 372 file(s) · 3779 bare -- token(s) …` |
| `check:pm-governed-merges` | 0 | self-test pass |
| `check:pm-skill-id-lint` | 0 | pass |
| `check:required-contexts` | 0 | six required contexts resolved |
| `check:nul-bytes` | 0 | `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 6711 text file(s) … no raw ASCII control bytes).` |
| `check:empty-changeset` | 0 | `✓ No empty-frontmatter changeset introduced by this diff` |

A control-byte self-scan over both changed files (`grep -naP` across the C0 range plus DEL) is clean independently of the gate. `check:required-contexts` first reported `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the dependency yaml is not installed`; that is the fresh-worktree case its own message describes, and it is recorded as green only after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and a re-run.

⚠️ `dispatch-gates.mjs` was run **without** a hand-supplied path list, so the change set is the merge-base three-dot one (`2 path(s) … committed 0, working tree 2, untracked 0`) and cannot pick up sibling PRs' files.
